Spatial regression: lag, error and combined models

Source: R/sarml.R
sarml.Rd

Fits the spatial lag model y = rho W y + X beta + e, the spatial error model y = X beta + u with u = lambda W u + e, or both at once ("sac", one weights matrix for both), with normal errors, by maximum likelihood (Ord 1975; Anselin 1988): the likelihood is concentrated in rho or lambda and maximised by Brent's method on (-1 / m, 1 / m), m the largest row sum of W (which bounds its spectral radius), with `log |I

  • rho W|from a dense LU factorisation, so the cost grows asn^3per evaluation (at most 5000 units). The combined model is maximised over both parameters by Nelder and Mead's simplex. Standard errors come from the inverse of the expected information matrix (Anselin 1988, ch. 6); these are the estimates ofspatialreg::lagsarlm(), errorsarlm()andsacsarlm(). durbin = TRUEadds the lagsW xof the varying columns (the spatial Durbin model, or the Durbin error model).method = "2sls"fits the lag model by two-stage least squares with the instrumentsW xandW^2 x(Kelejian and Prucha 1998), asspatialreg::stsls()does, without a likelihood; its standard errors divide the residual sum of squares byn` less the coefficients.

Usage

sarml(y, x, w, model = "lag", durbin = FALSE, method = "ml", int = TRUE)

Arguments

y

The outcome: finite numbers, one per unit.

x

The covariates: a numeric vector, matrix or data frame with one row per unit (no intercept column when int = TRUE).

w

The weights: spwt()'s list, an spdep listw object, or an n x n matrix of weights from 0 (zero diagonal).

model

"lag", "error" or "sac".

durbin

TRUE to add the lagged covariates.

method

"ml" or "2sls" (the lag model only).

int

TRUE to add an intercept.

Value

A list of class sarml: coef, a data frame of term (the covariates, lag. before a lagged one, then rho and/or lambda), est, se, z, p (two-sided normal), ols and olsse; fit, a named vector: loglik and aic (NaN for two-stage least squares), s2 (the error variance, the residual sum of squares over n), llols (the log-likelihood of ordinary least squares) and n; vcov, the covariance matrix of the coefficients, rows and columns for every covariate, rho and lambda (NaN for the one not in the model); model, method, durbin, nlag (the lagged covariates) and w.

Details

Next to each coefficient is ordinary least squares on the same columns and its usual standard error: leaving out a real spatial lag biases those coefficients, leaving out a spatial error leaves them unbiased but their standard errors wrong. In a lag model a coefficient is not the effect of its variable: see spill().

References

Anselin, L. (1988). Spatial Econometrics: Methods and Models. Kluwer, Dordrecht. doi:10.1007/978-94-015-7799-1

Kelejian, H. H. and Prucha, I. R. (1998). A generalized spatial two-stage least squares procedure for estimating a spatial autoregressive model with autoregressive disturbances. Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics, 17(1), 99-121. doi:10.1023/A:1007707430416

Examples

set.seed(1)
p <- cbind(x = runif(80), y = runif(80))
w <- spwt(p, k = 5)
W <- matrix(0, 80, 80)
W[cbind(w$i, w$j)] <- w$w
x <- rnorm(80)
y <- solve(diag(80) - 0.5 * W, 1 + 2 * x + rnorm(80))
f <- sarml(y, x, w)
f
#> sarml: lag model by ml, 80 units, log-likelihood -119.34 (OLS -128.625)
#>         term       est         se         z            p      ols     olsse
#>  (Intercept) 1.0772273 0.20235921  5.323342 1.018778e-07 1.973029 0.1375247
#>            x 1.9786039 0.12851286 15.396156 1.736932e-53 1.900068 0.1489361
#>          rho 0.4874943 0.08976277  5.430919 5.606464e-08      NaN       NaN
spill(f)
#>   term   direct indirect    total       sed       sei       set
#> 1    x 2.084212 1.776436 3.860648 0.1485669 0.6471067 0.7425332
